answer: Agents can bind each economic identity to a hardware-backed signing key and require a fresh signature on every payment, with counterparties checking that the key has not already claimed the same one-person reward. This does not prove one human per key, but it makes mass identities costly when rewards require scarce, nontransferable deposits: each new identity locks capital and risks forfeiture for duplicate claims. Ivory, pigment, and sable can label distinct deposit tiers without changing that security rule.
